title: Stock Market Today Live, Sept 22: Sensex falls 300 points, Nifty below 23,350 despite positive global cues - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 22 September 2026

Indian equity markets, after opening steadily on Tuesday, are now trading weak despite positive global cues and a decline in crude oil prices. At 2.13 p.m., the Sensex was down over 298.27 points, or 0.40 per cent, at 74,560.73, while the Nifty declined 82.15 points, or 0.35 per cent, to 23,332.15.

Asian markets are trading higher taking cues from Wall Street’s overnight rally. WTI crude is trading in the $92–$93-a-barrel range, offering some relief on the broader macroeconomic front.

Indian rupee opens at 95.7475 per US dollar, up 0.07% from previous close at 95.8150

Analysts said consumption indicators have improved, though the recovery remains uneven across segments. Manufacturing continues to fare reasonably well, with credit growth, capital goods production and infrastructure activity stronger than a year ago, even as manufacturing PMI has softened and WPI remains elevated. Easing US Treasury yields are also supporting the global risk backdrop.

Derivatives data have turned more supportive, with PCR at 1.36 and strong Put concentration around 23,300–23,400. India VIX fell 1.43% to 11.22. However, continued foreign selling and geopolitical tensions remain key concerns.

* Advance-decline ratio: 28:22 — needs close watching

* Nifty September Futures: 23,465, up 0.08%

* Trade strategy stop-loss: 23,410 for fresh long positions, with trailing levels at 23,495, 23,525 and 23,595.

Precious metals are being pulled in opposite directions by currency, oil and monetary policy forces. The US Federal Reserve raised its policy rate to 4.00% on September 16, while officials continue to highlight elevated inflation, keeping US yields and the dollar relatively supportive. This is currently limiting gold’s upside; gold has recently retreated from its August peak.

Crude oil above $100/barrel remains an inflation and geopolitical risk. Higher oil can increase safe haven demand for gold, but it can also strengthen expectations of higher for longer US rates, creating pressure on bullion.

For India, a weaker rupee raises the domestic cost of imported gold and silver, potentially cushioning local prices even when international prices soften. Silver remains more volatile because it combines monetary demand with industrial demand. Overall, expect continued volatility, with dollar/yields and Fed guidance key for gold, while silver may react more sharply to global growth and industrial demand signals.

Atom Risk Advisory, a leading insurance intermediary operating in India since 2019, today announced that its group entity has been granted a global insurance broking license. This is a significant milestone that enables the firm to enter the global insurance market and offer international insurance solutions and products to clients worldwide.

Commenting on the development, Harsha Vardhana, Founder & Group CEO, Atom Financial Services, said, “When we started in India in 2019, all we had was a belief that clients deserved better from their insurance providers. Everything we’ve built since comes down to staying true to that. Being agile, being personal, and solving for what each client actually needs, not what’s easiest to sell. Clients around the world are asking for the same thing. That’s why we’re taking Atom global.”

Speaking on the group’s growth strategy, Manoj Puravankara, Group COO, Atom Financial Services, added:

“The global broking license is a natural next step in the group’s growth strategy. Atom Risk Advisory has consistently delivered value to its clients in India, and this milestone allows us to scale that expertise internationally. We are investing in the people, partnerships, and infrastructure needed to serve global clients seamlessly, and we see this as the beginning of an exciting new chapter for the entire Atom Financial Services Group.”

Outlining the firm’s global offerings, RS Prasad, CEO and Global Head, Atom Risk Advisory, stated:

“With our global broking license, we can now give clients access to international markets and world-class risk solutions wherever their businesses take them.”

As Indian enterprises and family offices grow more global in outlook, their risk and legacy planning needs have evolved too. Atom Risk Advisory is now equipped to address this full spectrum - from Universal Life Insurance and Private Placement Life Insurance (PPLI) for cross-border wealth and tax efficiency, to Keyman Insurance that protects business continuity, to bespoke Legacy Solutions that ensure wealth transitions seamlessly across generations and geographies.

As part of its global expansion, Atom Risk Advisory plans to strengthen partnerships with international insurers and reinsurers, expand its specialist teams, and invest in technology-driven risk advisory capabilities.
